key_insight: A lightweight probabilistic bias-correction layer can substantially improve 2–6 week (subseasonal) forecasts from both AI and physics-based dynamical models by correcting persistent errors and producing calibrated uncertainty estimates.
problem_solved: Subseasonal forecast skill degrades sharply at 2–6 week lead times due to compounding model errors and persistent biases, leaving decision-makers with unreliable point forecasts and poorly quantified uncertainty.
method: Learn historical forecast errors from ensembles of dynamical and AI models and model those errors probabilistically (e.g., quantile mapping / distributional correction).
Apply learned corrections to raw model outputs to produce calibrated predictive distributions instead of biased point forecasts.
Integrate with existing forecast pipelines as a post-processing layer, enabling improved ensemble spread, reliability (PIT/calibration), and skill across subseasonal leads.
impact: This approach gives AI/ML practitioners a practical, model-agnostic post-processing tool to boost subseasonal forecast accuracy and uncertainty quantification—improving decision support for agriculture, water/energy management, and hazard response.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: raw dynamical & AI forecasts → probabilistic bias-correction module → calibrated forecast distributions.
Map series showing before/after forecast skill (e.g., anomaly correlation or CRPS) for weeks 2–6.
Reliability diagram or PIT histogram comparing calibrated vs. uncalibrated forecasts.
Bar/line chart of skill vs. lead time illustrating reduced degradation across subseasonal horizons.
paper_title: Enhancing AI and Dynamical Subseasonal Forecasts with Probabilistic Bias Correction
paper_authors: Hannah Guan, Soukayna Mouatadid, Paulo Orenstein, Judah Cohen, Haiyu Dong
